slice: Rates rise, IPOs pause, hedges lock in. Calm is now a luxury.

callouts.text: major central banks have raised rates since Q2, up from 2 in Q1, the IMF reports.
strategic sale in a decade: IDBI Bank would be India’s biggest at ₹52,878 crore.

stories.title: IMF: three risks keep global finance on edge
points: The IMF says markets have stayed resilient since April, but risks to financial stability are still elevated. It names three: a sharp correction in AI-linked stocks, a sudden rise in government bond yields, and cyber attacks.

Policy is turning: 14 of 33 major central banks have raised rates since the second quarter, against 2 in the first. In its stress test, bank capital would fall about 1.5 points, yet weak banks now hold 22% of global bank assets.
Its advice is to curb leverage behind the AI boom, steady public debt, and strengthen cyber defences.
numbers: major central banks hiked since Q2
of bank assets held by weak banks
stories.why: Calm prices can hide thin cushions. If AI valuations fall just as yields jump, borrowers, banks and funds all feel it together.
stories.other: Banks overall pass the stress test, and the IMF rates the AI risk as unchanged since April, so this is a warning about weak spots rather than a forecast of a crash.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: the IMF’s three risks (AI correction, bond yield spike, cyber attack), the rise in central bank rate hikes and what it urges.

stories.title: IDBI sale would be India’s 13th strategic disinvestment
points: The proposed ₹52,878 crore sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax would be the government’s 13th strategic disinvestment in a decade, and its largest, ahead of HPCL (₹36,915 crore) and Air India.

Not every deal brought in cash. Some were transfers between state-owned firms, one raised no exchequer proceeds, and of Air India’s ₹18,000 crore price the Tatas paid ₹2,700 crore in cash and took over ₹15,300 crore of debt.
stories.why: Headline sale values can overstate what reaches the government, so watch the cash component and what the buyer takes on.
stories.other: What to watch: whether the Fairfax deal closes and how much of the price is cash. Private owners may also run weak state firms better, which is part of the policy case.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: why IDBI Bank would be India’s 13th and largest strategic sale, and why headline values flatter the cash received.

stories.title: RBI rules turn rupee hedging from a trade into a commitment
points: ET Prime explains what the RBI’s 10 October rules mean for company treasurers. A cancelled forward hedge can no longer be rebooked, so hedging is now a commitment, not a running trade.
For importers, large hedges cost more because banks must park a 20% cash reserve with the RBI. Bigger hedges also need more paperwork.
The piece argues waiting is not free either: companies that delayed hedging last month already paid for it.
numbers: cash reserve on large importer hedges
stories.why: Finance heads must now decide once, and live with it. Policies built on cancelling and rebooking hedges need rewriting.
stories.other: Rolling over a contract is still allowed, and the rules aim at speculation rather than ordinary hedging. The cost may ease if the rupee steadies.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: how the RBI’s new rules make rupee hedging a commitment and what it means for the hedge-or-wait decision.

stories.title: Boden: AI agents will bypass banking apps, so banks must engage
points: Starling’s founder and former chief executive argues that the next phase of banking will not be a better app but an AI agent acting between banks and customers.

Banks have spent years building defences that insist on a human, and fraud systems tuned to human behaviour would flag an agent working around the clock. Meta’s Muse agent drew 6.6mn downloads in two weeks.
She calls for banks, regulators and AI firms to meet, welcoming authorised agents while keeping rogue ones out.
stories.why: If customers hand routine money tasks to agents, the bank that controls how agents connect keeps the relationship, and others become plumbing.
stories.other: This is one founder’s view. Banks have real fraud and liability reasons to move slowly, as the JPMorgan story below shows.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: Anne Boden’s case that AI agents will replace banking apps and what banks must change.

stories.title: JPMorgan blocks unvetted AI agents from customer accounts
points: JPMorgan will not let unvetted outside AI agents log in to or operate customer accounts, a spokeswoman confirmed. Agents can see balances read-only through approved connectors such as Plaid, but cannot use customer credentials, move money or pay bills.
On the earnings call Jamie Dimon said: “You don’t want rogue agents, and there could be thousands of them.” He framed it as a question of who bears the losses.
No timeline was given for any change.
stories.why: This is the other side of the Boden argument: the biggest US bank wants agents to arrive on its terms, with liability settled first.
stories.other: What to watch: whether customer demand for agents pushes the bank to open up, and whether rivals take a looser line.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: what outside AI agents can and cannot do on JPMorgan customer accounts.

stories.title: Australia’s biggest IPO in 30 years is cancelled amid AI jitters
points: Data-centre firm Firmus cancelled a planned raise of almost $5bn, which would have been Australia’s largest IPO in 30 years, citing market volatility. It plans a private raise and a US listing next year.
Airtrunk and SoftBank’s SB Energy have also delayed, and timing for the Anthropic and OpenAI listings is uncertain. Rising rates, jumpy markets and local backlash to data centres are blamed.
Nscale still hopes to list within weeks.
stories.why: AI infrastructure needs cheap, plentiful capital. If listings stall, unproven builders feel it first, and that links back to the IMF’s warning about leverage behind the boom.
stories.other: What to watch: whether Nscale lists on schedule, and whether Anthropic’s investor day restores confidence.
stories.imageAlt: KKReckons explainer: why Firmus cancelled its IPO and which AI infrastructure listings are waiting.
